blocks.text: 90. Therefore by newness of the spirit is our calling, and not in the oldness of the letter; [^irenaeus-demonstration-iv-221] even as Jeremiah prophesied: Behold the days come, saith the Lord, that I will accomplish for the house of Israel and for the house of Judah the covenant: of the testament [^irenaeus-demonstration-iv-222] which I covenanted with their fathers, in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt: because they continued not in the covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord. For this is the covenant of the testament that I will covenant with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord: I will put my laws [^irenaeus-demonstration-iv-223] into their minds, and write them in their hearts; and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people: and they shall not teach any more every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for all shall know me, from the least to the greatest of them. For I will pardon and be merciful unto the sins of their iniquities, and their sins will I remember no more.

irenaeus-demonstration-iv-221.text: I have followed the simple emendation suggested by the editors: the printed text has “not in our oldness.”

irenaeus-demonstration-iv-222.text: After διαθήκην the words καινήν, οὐ κατὰ τὴν διαθήκην must have been missed by the scribe or translator. “The covenant of the testament” is only a double rendering of διαθήκην : such double renderings occur several times in this quotation, but I have not retained them in every case.

irenaeus-demonstration-iv-223.text: Lit. “giving my laws”; cf. Heb. viii. 10 .
